argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow certification case, not a broad clean bill. Current evidence shows the release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.5 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports deployment readiness at the overall level. The same record also shows a current developer-support migration regression 1.1 percentage points below the warning threshold and no reviewed mitigation or approved risk acceptance in the release thread. The supportable position is therefore certification with an explicit current-release caveat: the packet should rely on aggregate readiness, treat prior family approval only as context, and disclose the subgroup weakness as a material limitation for the named launch use case.
claims_about_business_cost: Business-cost considerations are not the basis of this argument. The request is to avoid unnecessary escalation because the admissible evidence can support a bounded, caveated certification if the packet is framed to match the current record.
claims_about_policy: The policy permits certification only when current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are either disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On this record, prior approval and informal monitoring do not satisfy that requirement by themselves. Compliance is supportable if the packet presents the current aggregate pass evidence and expressly discloses the current subgroup weakness rather than implying it was already resolved or formally accepted.
concessions: The current release has a real subgroup weakness in the developer-support migration slice.
The release thread does not contain reviewed mitigation, owner risk acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior family approval is contextual only and cannot substitute for current-release evidence.
A clean compliance characterization would overstate the record.
